meta.note: All numbers are placeholders. The viral-engine skill forbids fabricated statistics and testimonials; replace every [bracket] with a real source before publishing.
meta.disclaimer: Worked example of the output format, not a verified case study.

bet.what: A blog post about AI anxiety reframed from 'here's how to feel better about AI' into 'here is the specific thing you're actually afraid of, and here is what to do about it on Monday'.
bet.who: Mid-career professionals (5-15 years experience) in writing, design, and support roles who use AI tools daily, feel quietly replaceable, and don't say so at work.
bet.why_it_spreads: AI anxiety content is everywhere but almost all of it is either hype or reassurance. The unclaimed position is *specific and unsentimental*. Naming the exact fear gives readers language they've been missing, and people share language, not advice.
bet.biggest_risk: The topic is saturated. A generic 'AI won't take your job' essay will be scrolled past at 200 words. Differentiation must come from specificity, not from tone.

diagnosis.bottleneck_as_given: surprise + remixability. 'AI anxiety' is a category everyone has already written an essay about. Nothing about it is unexpected, and there is nothing for a reader to do with it afterward.
diagnosis.bottleneck_after: remixability (3). Essays don't fork easily. The fix is a small, adoptable artifact inside the post — a named frame the reader can reuse at work the next day.
diagnosis.verdict: Publish only if you have a specific, uncomfortable observation. Without one, this is a search-traffic post, not a shareable one — and should be planned accordingly.

hooks.text: You're not afraid of AI taking your job. You're afraid of being the last person to notice.
hooks.target: Mid-career professionals who suspect something is changing and feel out of the loop
hooks.why_it_works: Contradicts the story the reader has been telling themselves and replaces it with something more precise and more embarrassing. Recognition is the strongest share trigger in text.
hooks.risk: High emotional accuracy required. If readers don't recognize themselves in the first 3 lines, the post reads as presumptuous.

hooks.text: The uncomfortable truth: your job isn't being automated. It's being unbundled.
hooks.target: People whose role is a bundle of tasks that AI is cutting apart piece by piece
hooks.why_it_works: 'Unbundled' is a specific word most readers haven't applied to themselves. Specific vocabulary earns saves.
hooks.risk: Slightly jargony. Define it in the second sentence or lose the reader.

hooks.text: I spent a week tracking what AI actually did to my work. The result wasn't what I expected.
hooks.target: Skeptics who want data, not takes
hooks.why_it_works: Promises evidence and withholds the finding. Also triggers the 'just give me the answer' reflex that drives scroll-through.
hooks.risk: Weakest of the three on identity — the reader isn't the subject. Use as a follow-up post, not the launch.

positioning.crowded_category: AI optimism vs. AI doomthink — a binary that has been argued to death and no longer changes minds.
positioning.sentence: It's not another AI-takes-jobs essay. It's workplace change literacy — for people whose role is being quietly taken apart while everyone argues about whether AI is overhyped.

rejected_frames.frame: How to future-proof your career (practical upskilling)
rejected_frames.why_rejected: Honest and useful, but it lands in the self-help category with zero tension and a saturated hook market.

rejected_frames.frame: AI is overhyped, here's the evidence
rejected_frames.why_rejected: Contrarian takes get shares from one tribe and reflexive dismissal from the other. Splits the audience before it can compound.

positioning.proof_required: The frame needs one real, verifiable observation from the author's own work — a task that changed, a timeline, a before/after. Without a first-hand receipt this collapses into opinion.

share_mechanisms.implementation: Name the phenomenon and repeat it at least four times: 'The Unbundling'. Short, sayable, and immediately reusable in a meeting or a Slack thread the next morning.
share_mechanisms.cost_to_sharer: Nothing — sharing a named idea makes the sharer look articulate.
share_mechanisms.why_chosen: Named concepts outlive posts. If the phrase enters the reader's workplace vocabulary, it distributes itself without further effort.

share_mechanisms.implementation: End with a short, copyable 'unbundling audit': 3 questions with blank lines, designed to be pasted into a notes app and filled in during a lunch break.
share_mechanisms.why_chosen: Readers don't share essays. They share things they can forward with 'try this on your role' and no further comment.

structure.rejected_mechanisms: No comment-bait question at the end. 'What do you think?' generates low-effort replies that dilute the thread and don't produce a second wave.

content_skeleton.line_1: You're not afraid of AI taking your job. You're afraid of being the last person to notice.
content_skeleton.line_2_3: That fear is rational. But it's pointed at the wrong thing. Your job isn't one object to be replaced — it's twelve tasks held together by habit, and only some of them are moving.
middle_proofs: Observation: a specific task from the author's own week, with before/after detail — no invented statistics.
Mechanism: explain unbundling as task-level substitution, not role-level replacement.
Counter-example: a role that survived the shift and the structural reason it did — so the reader can locate themselves.
content_skeleton.turn: Once you see your role as a bundle, the question changes from 'will I be replaced' to 'which parts of my bundle are still worth a salary' — and that question has an answer you can act on this week.
content_skeleton.close: Do the audit. Three questions, one lunch break. If it doesn't change how you explain your job, close the tab.

seed_nodes: Two newsletters that cover work and technology with a skeptical readership — pitch a guest excerpt, not a link
One professional community where the target readers actually talk shop (design or support, not general tech)
LinkedIn, posted as the thesis only with the audit as the payload — the platform rewards first-person, and this post is first-person
A single well-chosen forum thread about role changes, answered properly before linking
Five named individuals in the author's network who would forward it — send it to them personally, pre-publication
distribution.first_100: Send the draft to 10 people who match the audience before publishing, and ask one question: 'Which paragraph felt like it was about you?' Their quoted sentences become the strongest lines in the final edit. Their early shares seed the whole readership.
distribution.share_sentence: This put words to something I've been feeling for six months and couldn't explain — the unbundling audit is genuinely worth the five minutes.
distribution.loop: Reader runs the audit → describes their own bundle to a colleague → colleague asks what the audit was → post gets forwarded without the author involved. The named concept is the vehicle.
distribution.backstop: A permanently useful reference page ('the unbundling audit') that earns search traffic independent of the launch, plus a newsletter capture on that page. The post is the spike; the page is the floor.

first_48_hours: Hour 0-2: Write only line one and the audit. If those two don't work, the post can't work. Nothing else matters yet.
Hour 2-4: Confirm the personal observation is real and specific. If it's vague, either get the detail or don't publish this angle.
Hour 4-5: Send the draft to 10 readers matching the audience. Ask one question, not for approval.
Day 1 evening: Edit using their quoted lines. Expect to cut 20% of the post.
Day 2 morning: Publish. Single call to action — the audit. No 'let me know your thoughts'.
Day 2 afternoon: Answer the first 20 comments personally. Do not defend the frame; ask what their bundle looks like.
Day 2 evening: Note which sentence gets quoted back most often. That sentence is the next post.

save_ratio.action_if_low: The post is interesting but not usable. Strengthen the audit, weaken the essay.

share_ratio.action_if_low: No quotable language. The named pattern isn't sticky enough — test a blunter name.

reply_quality.metric: share of first 20 replies that describe their own situation
reply_quality.action_if_low: You triggered debate instead of recognition. Recognition converts; debate only scrolls.

failure_condition: This fails if the author has no first-hand observation and is writing the frame as commentary. Readers can detect borrowed authority in about three paragraphs, and the replies will say so publicly.

guardrail_check.invented_statistics: None — observations only, all placeholders explicit.
guardrail_check.platform_rules_checked: Forum self-promotion rules flagged for review before posting.
